Abstract:
This study attempts at undertaking a comprehensive study of personal names among
Ghanaian Hausa. It particularly looks at the socio-pragmatic usage of the Hausa
names.

names. This paper argues that the Hausa give names to their children by considering
the social, cultural, and religious philosophy of the Hausa speech community.

philosophy behind these Hausa naming practices goes a long way to help in the
peculiar identity of the Ghanaian Hausa.

3.10 The Transformation of Kunya Names into Personal Names
In Islamic and Arab naming traditions, kunya (patronymic or
teknonym) refers to a name that begins with Abu (“Father of”) or
Umm (“Mother of”), followed by the name of a child or
something closely associated with the individual.

y the name of a child or
something closely associated with the individual.

While the most
common form derives from one’s firstborn son, a kunya may also

trait, habit, or something a person loves.
The kunya served not only as a form of respect but also as an
affectionate alternative to the given name (ism).

possessive-based, diminutive, and verb-derived nicknames
reflects a deep connection between language, identity, and lived
experiences.

continue to evolve, blending tradition with contemporary
